title: Rename qwen parser to xmlfunc and wire jsonrepair into XML parameter …
body:
…parsing

The <function=name><parameter=key>value</parameter></function> tool-call format was popularized by Qwen-Coder but has since been adopted by other model lineages (notably NVIDIA Nemotron-3 Super, whose chat template carries the same markers). Naming the parser after a single lineage was misleading, so the package is renamed to describe the wire format instead.

Detection in the new package now prioritizes the chat-template markers over the Qwen-specific architecture/name fallbacks, since the markers are the cross-lineage signal.

While in there, parameter values that look like JSON are now run through jsonrepair instead of plain encoding/json. Real-world Nemotron output was emitting JSON containing \033 ANSI escapes (invalid as a JSON escape), which caused json.Unmarshal to fail and the value to be stored as a raw string — downstream schema validators then rejected the call. The same two json.Unmarshal sites in the gemma parser were swapped for the same reason.

To make jsonrepair handle this case beyond the existing Gemma <|"|> quote-block path, normalize() gained normalizeInvalidStringEscapes which walks JSON strings and double-escapes any backslash sequence that is not a legal JSON escape (\033 -> \\033, etc.).

A regression test in xmlfunc/toolparse_test.go reproduces the failing Nemotron call.
